subject: Transportation Systems
title: Railways and Empire
description: A fast breakdown of Railways and Empire for builders.

hook.text: European empires didn't just build railways at home. They laid track across Africa and Asia.

buildup.text: Colonial railways hauled minerals to ports for export. They rarely connected local communities.

discovery.text: In Africa, rail lines ran from mines straight to the coast. Inland towns were deliberately bypassed.

twist.text: After independence, many nations inherited networks designed to serve someone else's economy.

climax.text: Fixing those networks—or building new ones—remains a massive infrastructure challenge today.

punchline.text: Colonial rails were built to extract, not connect.

quiz.question: Why were colonial railways often unhelpful for independent nations?
options: They connected mines to ports, not communities
